title: Geometric regularity of a stalk over a field gives smoothness near that point
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $z\in Z$. If the local $k$-algebra $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then there exists an open subscheme $V\subseteq Z$ containing $z$ for which $g|_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The $k$-algebra structure on the stalk is induced by $g$. No perfectness of $k$, closedness of $z$, or separability of $\kappa(z)/k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 038U (lemma-geometrically-regular-at-point), (3) implies (1), and Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), geometric regularity at z implies smoothness at z; smoothness at a point means smoothness on an open neighbourhood.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $z$ from the finite-type affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; write $\mathfrak p$ for $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ via $a/s\mapsto a_zs_z^{-1}$. This is a $k$-algebra isomorphism, since both structure maps take $c\in k$ to the germ of $g^*c$. Thus $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is geometrically regular. Set $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with residue map $\rho:A\to K$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The finite-type residue-field theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated], applied to $k\to A$ and $\mathfrak p$, gives that $K/k$ is finitely generated as a field.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), affine reduction; Tag 038U (lemma-geometrically-regular-at-point), local-ring formulation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] to the geometrically regular Noetherian $k$-algebra $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and the finitely generated field extension $K/k$. It gives that $C=K\otimes_k A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular ring: every prime localization of $C$ is a regular local ring. Noetherianity of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is already included in the geometric-regularity hypothesis.

Put $B=K\otimes_k A$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives the $K$-algebra map $\epsilon:B\to K$, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\lambda\rho(a)$. It is surjective since $\epsilon(\lambda\otimes1)=\lambda$. Hence $\mathfrak q=\ker\epsilon$ is maximal and its contraction under $j:A\to B$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, is $\mathfrak p$, because $\epsilon(j(a))=\rho(a)$ and $\ker\rho=\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $k$, then $1\otimes a_1,\ldots,1\otimes a_n$ generate $B$ over $K$: expand $a$ as a polynomial and expand tensors additively. Thus $B$ is finite type over $K$.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), base-changed finite-type algebra; rational-point variant using Tag 0381

proof.text: Let $W=\{1\otimes s:s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p\}\subset B$. Base change of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], with base ring $A$, gives $C\cong W^{-1}B$ as $B$-algebras (the identification is $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto b(1\otimes a)/(1\otimes s)$). Every $1\otimes s\in W$ has nonzero image $\rho(s)$ under $\epsilon$, so $\mathfrak q\cap W=\emptyset$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak qC$ is prime, contracts to $\mathfrak q$, and $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong C_{\mathfrak r}$. Since $C$ is regular by step 2, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization); Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization); local-ring identification used in Tag 038U

proof.text: The residue field at $\mathfrak q$ is $K$ as a $K$-algebra: on $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ the map is $[b/t]\mapsto\epsilon(b)/\epsilon(t)$; its inverse sends $\lambda$ to $[(\lambda\otimes1)/1]$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These are inverse because $b-(\epsilon(b)\otimes1)\in\mathfrak q$, and $\epsilon(t)\ne0$ for $t\notin\mathfrak q$. Therefore $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/K$ is separable: its only intermediate field is $K$, with empty transcendence basis and separable degree-one minimal polynomials [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), separable-residue-field requirement; explicit rational-point calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth] over the field $K$ to the finite-type $K$-algebra $B$ at $\mathfrak q$: step 4 gives regularity and step 5 gives the required separable residue field. Thus $K\to B$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-field-extension-descent] to $K/k$, $A$, and $\mathfrak q$; its contracted prime is $\mathfrak p$ by step 3. It supplies $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $A_f$ is a smooth $k$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth); Tag 02UQ (lemma-smooth-field-change-local); the final two inferences of Tag 038X

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ identifies with the open subscheme $D(f)$ of $U$. Its image $V\subset Z$ is open and contains $z$ because $f\notin\mathfrak p$. The structure morphism of this open subscheme is induced by $k\to A_f$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] and step 6 show that $g|_V$ is smooth. This is the required neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); affine smoothness: Morphisms Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), with Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth)

The delivery is one commit with two files (the report and the item); there are no new nodes and no repair note. The statement is unchanged from the live unsplit node. It matches Stacks 038X, smoothness at x from geometric regularity at x, with the hypothesis in the local-ring form of 038U(3). I read 038U, 038X, 00TV and 02UQ in literature/stacks-project. The proof follows a correct agent variant of 038X. Instead of choosing k' by 030R, it base-changes to K=kappa(p), which is finitely generated over k (finite-type residue node with R=k, prime (0)), so 0381 gives that K tensor A_p is regular. It then takes the K-rational point q=ker(epsilon), lambda tensor a maps to lambda rho(a), whose contraction is p. Localization base change (00DK) plus the prime-correspondence node identify B_q with a localization of C at qC, so B_q is regular local. Since kappa(q)=K, the residue extension is trivially separable. 00TV gives K to B smooth at q, 02UQ descends this to some f outside p with A_f smooth over k, and the open immersion for D(f) plus the 01V6/02H6 node finish the proof. I opened every cited statement and its hypotheses match. The only unwritten identification is tensor associativity, (K tensor_k A) tensor_A A_p = K tensor_k A_p, which is one line. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Duplicate search with rg -L for 038U/038X found only the global field criterion and support-only mentions; none states this pointwise result. The parent node lem-per-lfp-regular-stalk-smooth-neighborhood cites the item exactly as stated. I accept the five declared tool_uses (sk-thm-p1 nodes for 0381, 00E3, 00TV, 02UQ and 01V6), all generic commutative algebra. Edge cases checked: empty Z; generic point of affine space; the closed point x^p=t of A^1 over F_p(t), where the proof works; Spec k[x]/(x^p-t), which correctly fails the hypothesis.
